medhx: Hypertension, Chronic kidney disease, Osteoarthritis, Benign prostatic hyperplasia

note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for prior prostate cancer diagnosis with rising PSA and biopsy-confirmed disease.

Long-standing referral for prostate cancer management. The patient is a 67-year-old retired farmer, married, living with an adult child in a multi-generational household. He has a history of hypertension, chronic kidney disease, osteoarthritis, and benign prostatic hyperplasia. Medications include amlodipine, valsartan, lisinopril, metoprolol, and tamsulosin. He consumes 7 units of alcohol weekly and enjoys hiking on weekends. Recent gastroenterology surveillance colonoscopy was unremarkable. Mobility is limited, requiring a frame, and he prefers ground-floor consultations. PSA has risen from 1.8 ng/mL in Nov 2023 to 6.0 ng/mL in Feb 2025. Biopsy confirmed Gleason 3+4, ISUP GG2 disease with perineural invasion.
On DRE, the prostate is non-palpable, consistent with cTx staging. General examination shows a well-nourished male with stable vital signs. No signs of metastatic disease.

admin: Mobility limitation (frame); ground-floor consult room preferred.
